profile_text.body:
Databricks, founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, describes itself as a unified data and AI platform for enterprises. Its site presents the platform as covering ETL, data warehousing, analytics, and AI workloads on a single open and governed foundation, with the stated goal of allowing organizations to run both analytical and operational workloads without copying data or adding complexity. Key components the company highlights include Lakebase, described as a database that merges Postgres-style transactional capabilities with data lakehouse scale and governance; Databricks Genie, a conversational analytics interface that lets business users query enterprise data in plain language without SQL; and Unity Gateway, positioned as a multi-AI governance and cost control layer for managing access, spend, and observability across agents, models, and tools.

On the AI product side, Databricks offers DBRX, an open-source large language model built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture and oriented toward enterprise training use cases. The broader Databricks AI offering incorporates DBRX alongside MLflow for model governance and Unity Catalog for data governance, forming what the company calls a Lakehouse AI approach. The site also describes natural language dashboard creation and conversational analytics through Genie as part of what it characterizes as a next generation of business intelligence built on AI.

The site's held facts show 175 legal matters with California law exposure, consistent with the company's San Francisco headquarters, though no specific cases are detailed in the available data. Databricks is recorded as a for-profit startup with a dedicated presence on theworldofai.org.
